open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes
open_points.text: “module:surface turns every JSON text a request carries … into its canonical form with canonical_values.canonical_bytes” but the operation input is “One JSON value” and it must refuse “a duplicate key.”
open_points.question: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text or a representation that preserves duplicate members, and which component detects duplicate keys before ordinary JSON decoding loses them?
options: Accept raw JSON text and parse it while rejecting duplicate members
Accept a duplicate-preserving JSON syntax tree
Accept an ordinary decoded value, making duplicate-key refusal impossible in this operation
open_points.default_guess: Accept raw JSON text at the surface boundary and reject duplicate members while parsing.

open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case
open_points.text: Its inputs are “input values by port, optional expected outputs,” while trial cases may contain file fixtures and trial_case_added must publish their bytes through store.put_value_bytes.
open_points.question: For authored file inputs and expected file outputs, does the operation receive file bytes, file facts, a transport attachment, or an existing value reference?
options: Receive the file bytes with their declared port
Receive file facts plus bytes through a separate attachment mechanism
Receive an existing StoredValue reference
open_points.default_guess: Receive file bytes as part of the authored case request and derive their digest, size and media type.

open_points.subject: trial execution output size
open_points.text: sandbox.execute_function applies only the contract’s output_bytes bound, while M07 allows detail_code value_too_large and record_trial_execution stores successful value outputs; functions.try_implementation and functions.submit_implementation do not say what happens when a successful trial value exceeds stored_value_bytes_max.
open_points.question: How is an otherwise successful trial or admission execution classified when one value output exceeds stored_value_bytes_max, and is any output stored?
options: Record contract_violation with detail_code value_too_large and store no oversized output
Record resource_exhausted
Keep the successful execution without storing the oversized value
Treat the later store failure as internal_error
open_points.default_guess: Record contract_violation with value_too_large and do not store that execution’s outputs.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances
open_points.text: It says an unreadable manifest record “or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5)” stops startup, but the operation has no operation name or proposed ports with which to perform A08’s operation-specific checks.
open_points.question: Which exact A08 checks are performed at startup, and are all capability entries validated or only the service and selected-instance structure needed for the credential-header collision check?
options: Validate only service-level and selected-instance facts used by this operation
Validate every capability entry using the checks that do not require proposed ports
Do not validate capability entries at startup
open_points.default_guess: Validate only the service record structure, capability-name uniqueness, and selected-instance facts needed for the header-collision check.

open_points.subject: store.read_value_bytes
open_points.text: State 3 says “A spooled file whose run no longer holds its spool is refused,” while State 5 says “whether a run still holds its spool is checked by its caller” and “store trusts them.”
open_points.question: Does store.read_value_bytes itself enforce the run-spool lifecycle, or must it return lingering bytes whenever the caller supplies an existing SpooledFile identity?
options: The caller alone enforces spool eligibility; store only verifies the record and bytes
store.read_value_bytes independently checks whether the run still holds its spool
Both caller and store enforce the rule
open_points.default_guess: The caller enforces eligibility and store only resolves and verifies the named bytes.

open_points.subject: store entity updates and Run M19
open_points.text: Named changes say record_run_progress updates “the run’s status, outputs, WaitingPoints M20, ended_at, cancelled_by” and record_resumption adds a resumption, but the store convention says only lifecycle fields such as “a status, who decided or resolved or released and when, concluded_at” may change and “every other field is never changed.”
open_points.question: Are Run.outputs, Run.waiting and Run.resumptions mutable fields of the Run row, or must progress be represented in separate records and derived without changing them?
options: Allow all Run fields explicitly named by record_run_progress and record_resumption to update in place
Keep those Run fields immutable and derive them from separate records
Allow outputs and waiting to update but store resumptions separately
open_points.default_guess: Allow the Run fields explicitly named by the two named changes to update in place.

open_points.subject: functions.try_implementation response
open_points.text: The operation returns “One TrialExecution per case … outcome, output digests, pass or output_mismatch,” while “Records reach a caller as they are … with values resolved by module:surface,” and M07 names StoredValue outputs for value ports.
open_points.question: Does a direct try_implementation response include resolved value outputs, StoredValue references, or only output digests?
options: Return only output digests and file facts as the operation states
Return complete TrialExecution records with value outputs resolved by surface
Return TrialExecution records containing unresolved StoredValue references
open_points.default_guess: Return complete TrialExecution evidence with value outputs resolved under the disclosure rules and file outputs as facts only.
